stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: The disastrous diplomacy of Jared Kushner
stories.text: In a speech to the Israeli Knesset on October 13, 2025, President Trump spoke at length on how he would deploy his son-in-law Jared Kushner to secure peace deals in Gaza, Iran, and Ukraine. “ We always bring Jared when we wanna get that deal closed ,” Trump said. Prior to his work with the Trump White House, Kushner’s main professional experience was as a real estate developer. He almost bankrupted his family’s development company by purchasing an aging New York City skyscraper for $1.8 billion . After assuming a broad foreign policy portfolio during Trump’s first term, Kushner leveraged his connections with autocrats in the Middle East to raise billions for a new private equity company, Affinity Partners, in 2021. Kushner then pledged not to be involved in a second Trump White House. “ I’m an investor now ,” Kushner said in February 2024. “I served in government, and I think my track record is pretty impeccable. Now I’m a private investor.” Without explanation, Kushner broke that pledge and has been involved in nearly every consequential foreign policy negotiation since Trump returned to the White House in early 2025. stories.title: Democrats Declare War On Their Own Voters
stories.text: A deep blue wave is rising, and establishment Democrats are panicking. After progressive primary wins in New York , Colorado , and Michigan , the center-left’s headquarters, Third Way, announced a $15 million program to destroy the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA). Their president, speaking about the effort to The New York Times , said the organization is “preparing for the war that is coming.” As I wrote in The Lever a few weeks ago, centrist Democrats are taking the wrong lessons from the rise of populist economic candidates. As the GOP did in 2010, Democrats believe they can outmuscle their angry base. They cannot. Their plan seems almost designed to ensure that progressive and democratic socialist influence will continue to increase. Like so many historical examples, Third Way’s attempts to prevent their worst nightmare will only bring it closer to reality. Third Way’s mission, as stated at its conference earlier this year, is to be the group determining the terms of debate for the 2028 Democratic primary contest. stories.title: Live Wednesday: Israel's Lobby with Eli Clifton and Ian Lustick
stories.text: Corporate media treats Israel's lobby as the third rail of American politics. Eli Clifton and Ian Lustick didn't get the memo. This Wednesday, the authors of Israel's Lobby join Drop Site for a live conversation on how campaign cash and political pressure built one of the most powerful lobbying operations in Washington, and why crossing it can end careers. Drop Site's Ryan Grim and Murtaza Hussain host, and you'll get your questions answered by the group live. If you want to support the journalism holding Israel's lobby accountable, and get access to this event and future ones, upgrade today. Eli Clifton is an investigative journalist covering money in politics and U.S. foreign policy, and a cofounder of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft. His reporting has appeared in The Guardian, The Nation, The Intercept, Foreign Policy, and elsewhere. Ian Lustick is Professor Emeritus of Political Science at the University of Pennsylvania, where he held the Bess W. Heyman Chair, and has spent decades studying Israeli-Palestinian affairs and American foreign policy in the region. Want to read ahead or follow along?
